concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: complete desktop UI refactor concept sheet for a real Windows application implemented entirely in C with Win32 common controls, custom GDI drawing, and one D3D11 preview child window.

Primary request: Create four crisp front-on application-window mockups in a clean 2-by-2 grid. Each window is approximately 1040 by 700 logical pixels, compact enough for a normal desktop. The sheet is a professional engineering/product design reference, not a marketing illustration. Small captions outside the windows identify "Capture — Phone screen", "Devices", "Settings", and "Diagnostics". Add a small outside caption "UI CONCEPT — NOT A RUNNING BUILD".

Visual direction: compact, precise, professional dark Windows utility. Flat near-black and charcoal surfaces, thin straight gray dividers, high-contrast Segoe UI text, a restrained blue selection/action accent, amber for unavailable output. 1-pixel borders. Square or at most 2-pixel-radius client controls. Conventional dropdowns with visible arrow buttons, rectangular push buttons, native tab bars, checkboxes, table rows, vertical scrollbars. No bubble/soft look, no floating cards, no pill buttons or toggle switches, no gradients, no glass, no blur, no deep shadows, no oversized typography. Clearly visible enabled, selected, disabled and focused states. Every control must look faithfully implementable with HWND controls and straightforward C owner drawing. Do not invent focus/exposure/HDR controls.

Shared shell in all four windows: native Windows caption "Android Webcam Manager", ordinary minimize/maximize/close. A compact navigation tab row: "Capture", "Devices", "Settings", "Diagnostics". A slim bottom status strip with labeled states "ADB Connected", "Source Stopped" or "Source Receiving", "Camera Available", "Mic Not installed". Labels plus color, never color alone. Footer has the same right-aligned rectangular Start or Stop button.

Top-left Capture screen: Capture tab selected. Top form row has label Device, wide dropdown "Pixel 10 Pro XL", and small text "USB · Authorized". Second row has label Video source and dropdown "Phone screen". Main body splits roughly 70/30: large black 16:9 "Output preview" area on the left showing a tall portrait Android screen centered with substantial black pillarboxes, a neutral Settings-like screen with anonymous simple list items and no people or messages; right column contains real labeled controls "Display" dropdown "Built-in display · ID 0", "Profile" dropdown "Balanced · 1920 limit / 30 cap", "Orientation" dropdown "Follow phone", "Framing" dropdown "Fit — preserve all content", and "Audio" dropdown "Off". Show a small amber note "Phone microphone driver not installed". Beneath preview, compact text "Source: 864 × 1920 · updates vary" and "Requested output: 1920 × 1080 / 30", and rectangular "Hide preview". A plain bottom section separated by a straight rule reads "Windows camera" followed by "Android Webcam Camera (Windows Virtual Camera)" and a "Copy name" button; "Receiving app: Not checked" with "Test input" button. Small one-line notice "Entire phone display is captured, including notifications." The main action is "Stop". Do not depict touch control, web broadcasting, OBS, a cable, or a live call. Do not claim received microphone or receiver verification.

Top-right Devices screen: Devices tab selected, real report-style table columns Device, Connection, ADB state, Android. Rows: "Pixel 10 Pro XL | USB | Authorized | 17" selected; "Second Android phone | Wi-Fi | Unauthorized | —"; "Android emulator | Local | Offline | —". Plain selected-device detail fields beneath, no serials or addresses. Rectangular Refresh and Inspect buttons. A lower Wireless debugging section has Address:port edit, Pairing code masked edit, Pair and Connect buttons, and helper "Pairing and connection ports can differ." USB setup link/button. Overall source Stopped.

Bottom-left Settings screen: Settings tab selected with a second ordinary tab row "Output", "Dependencies", "Advanced". Output selected. Plain aligned form fields: "Requested camera format" dropdown "1920 × 1080 / 30"; "Output framing" dropdown "Fit — preserve aspect ratio"; "Preview scaling" dropdown "EWA Lanczos sharp"; "Camera output scaling" dropdown "EWA Lanczos sharp"; "Rotate output" dropdown "0°"; checkbox "Mirror output" unchecked; checkbox "Reconnect selected device" unchecked. Adjacent compact output-components table: "Virtual camera | Installed | Configure", "Phone microphone | Not installed | Setup". Honest short amber explanation "A signed microphone driver is required." Small explanation "Capture changes apply on next Start. Preview scaling applies immediately." A rectangular "Apply" button. No large onboarding cards, no display brightness control, no arbitrary camera-image controls.

Bottom-right Diagnostics screen: Diagnostics tab selected. Plain compact table with headings "Stage", "Observed state", rows ADB Authorized, Source Phone screen, Capture No active session, Windows camera Enumerated, Microphone Not installed, Receiving app Not checked. A bordered read-only monospaced log area below, concise example messages "Capture stopped", "No phone audio forwarded", "Output component available". Footer rectangular buttons "Copy capture command" and "Export redacted diagnostics". No graphs or fabricated latency/quality measurements.

Composition: all four windows share exact geometry, typography and reusable Win32 control styling, clearly separated gutters, fully visible and uncropped, sharp legible text. Strong affordance and precise alignment. Avoid decorative device illustrations, logos, rounded module containers, browser chrome, impossible non-native interactions. Mockups are illustrative planned states; actual microphone remains unavailable.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: compact professional Windows desktop UI concept, faithfully implementable in C using Win32 native controls plus simple GDI owner drawing and an integrated D3D11 preview.

Create ONE large, front-on, fully visible app-window screenshot mockup, with a small caption outside: "ALTERNATIVE LIGHT CAPTURE VIEW — UI CONCEPT". Window title "Android Webcam Manager". Dimensions approximately 1040 x 700 logical pixels. Highly readable Segoe UI typography, sharp straight aligned edges, dense useful layout like a polished professional Windows utility. Light white/very pale gray surfaces, dark gray text, thin gray rules, blue selected tabs/primary action, amber for unavailable. All client controls square or maximum 2-pixel corner radius. No bubble/soft look, no rounded cards, no pills/toggle switches, no gradients, no blur, no glass, no deep shadows, no decorative illustrations. Real Win32 dropdown arrow buttons, rectangular push buttons, tab bar, checkboxes, readable label/value fields, visible focus rectangle. No HTML/mobile-app styling.

Shared navigation tab bar: Capture selected, Devices, Settings, Diagnostics.
Compact upper row: label Device; dropdown "Pixel 10 Pro XL"; small state "USB · Authorized"; rectangular "Refresh".
Second compact row: label Video source; dropdown "Phone camera". Source switching uses this ordinary selector; do not draw a pill switch.

Body: left roughly 70% contains a sharp 16:9 integrated "Output preview" showing an illustrative camera test card on a desk with colored patches and a printed word "CAMERA"; no people, no private messages. This is a mock preview, not a measurement. Right roughly 30% is a narrow aligned property column:
Camera dropdown "Rear · ID 0"
Profile dropdown "Standard · 1080p / 30"
Rotate output dropdown "0°"
Framing dropdown "Fit — preserve aspect ratio"
Audio dropdown "Off"
Unchecked checkbox "Mirror output"
Small text "H.264 · 16 Mbps" and a rectangular "Advanced…" button.
Do not depict exposure, focus, HDR, zoom, torch, fabricated image-quality metrics, or an installed microphone.

Below preview: "Source: 1920 × 1080" and "Preferred output: 1920 × 1080 / 30". Right aligned rectangular "Hide preview". Make Source and Preferred output clearly different.

Below a straight horizontal divider: two practical output rows.
"Windows camera" with read-only exact value "Android Webcam Camera (Windows Virtual Camera)" and rectangular "Copy name".
"Phone microphone" with amber read-only value "Not installed — signed driver required" and rectangular "Setup".
A small separate line "Receiving app: Not checked" with "Test input". No claim of Discord verification.
Bottom strip: "ADB Connected" | "Source Receiving" | "Camera Available" | "Mic Not installed". Use readable labels and small indicators, not standalone colored circles. Main right-aligned rectangular blue button "Stop capture". Keep all controls within the window, no overlapping controls, no cropped elements, no giant blank white onboarding section.

Prioritize clear action affordance, tightly spaced aligned rows, a stable bottom action location, and a design that can genuinely be rendered by Win32 C. The image is a proposed camera-mode layout; phone-screen mode reuses the shell and changes only the source-specific controls.

implementationCorrections: Use valid numeric address:port examples; the dark mockup's ':pair' text is invalid.
Use neutral gray for stopped/off; amber for missing dependencies; red only for failures.
Disable device and video-source selectors during active capture, with Stop to change source helper.
Treat generated preview dimensions and active states as illustrative, not physical observations.
Replace mockup gradients with flat COLORREF fills; use native focus/disabled states.
Label output format as Preferred output, and show actual camera requests and receiver negotiation separately.
